findings.comment: $(RDMA_CLIENT_LIBS) was added to the build rule for $(TLS_MODULE_NAME) (valkey-tls.so). The TLS module does not use RDMA and should not depend on libvalkey_rdma.a or RDMA libraries.
Line 343 already appends $(RDMA_LIBS) to FINAL_LIBS, so adding $(RDMA_LIBS) again on line 344 duplicates these flags in the link command.

When config.rdma is enabled, writeHandler is invoked synchronously before the client is appended to config.clients (which occurs at listAddNodeTail) and before config.liveclients is incremented. If writeHandler fails on the initial write, it calls freeClient(c), which performs listSearchKey(config.clients, c) and aborts on assert(ln != NULL).

In createClient, rdma is only assigned config.rdma when !is_cluster_client. In cluster mode, rdma remains 0, so cluster clients connect over standard TCP. However, resetClient and createClient check the global config.rdma, which prevents registering AE_WRITABLE on the event loop for those TCP sockets, stalling them. Furthermore, cluster helpers (fetchClusterConfiguration at line 1104, fetchClusterSlotsConfiguration at line 1217, and node config fetching at line 1832) hardcode 0 instead of config.rdma.

When executing the 'fcall' test, getValkeyContext is called with rdma = 0 instead of config.rdma. If benchmarking over RDMA against an endpoint that requires RDMA, loading the function script will attempt a standard TCP connection and fail.
